nodes.name: Arc-melting of ternary alloys
nodes.procedure: The ternary Ir_{1-x}Rh_xSb intermetallic alloys were prepared using the arc-melting method (see the Supporting Information for details).
nodes.source_text: The ternary Ir_{1-x}Rh_xSb intermetallic alloys were prepared using the arc-melting method (see the Supporting Information for details).

The electrocatalytic performance for HER of Ir1−xRhxSb was assessed by a typical electrochemical workstation with a three-electrode configuration in 0.5 m H2SO4. The linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curves of Ir1−xRhxSb are shown in Figure 4a. ... Specifically, the Ir1−xRhxSb alloy exhibits an overpotential of 104, 39, 22, and 68 mV with x = 0, 0.2, 0.3, and 0.4, respectively. ... The Ir1−xRhxSb alloy exhibits a Tafel slope of 85.5, 73.1, 71.8, and 47.6 mV dec−1 with x = 0, 0.2, 0.3, and 0.4, respectively. ... The Ir1−xRhxSb alloy possesses a Cdl of 2.1, 16.1, 19.8, and 5.6 mF cm−2 with x = 0, 0.2, 0.3, and 0.4, respectively. ... It is found that the Ir0.7Rh0.3Sb exhibits the smallest charge transfer resistance. ... The potential did not increase obviously for more than 55 h.
The HER activity of the Ir1−xRhxSb alloy was also measured in 1 m KOH, with results shown in Figures S25–S29 in the Supporting Information.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows block morphology for Ir1−xRhxSb alloys obtained by crushing single crystal.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) photos of the prepared Ir_{1-x}Rh_xSb alloys taken at various magnifications are shown in Figures S1–S4... the Ir_{1-x}Rh_xSb alloys exhibit a common block morphology, since the material was obtained by crushing the single crystal.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals random shape and size of Ir1−xRhxSb alloy consistent with SEM images.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A representative TEM image of Ir_{1-x}Rh_xSb alloy is shown in Figure 1a, where the sample exhibits random shape and size, in consistent with the SEM images.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM images of IrSb and Ir0.7Rh0.3Sb show clearly defined atoms with Sb (red balls) and Ir/Rh (green balls), matching [100] and [111] crystal planes with lattice spacings of 3.37 Å and 3.7 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular darkfiled (HAADF) STEM images of IrSb and Ir_{0.7}Rh_{0.3}Sb are shown in Figure 1b,c... The eye-catching lattice spacing in Figure 1b,c is measured to be 3.37 and 3.7 Å... matching well with the plane distance of indexed (100) and (-110) facets, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Element mapping shows homogeneous distribution of Ir, Rh, and Sb over Ir0.7Rh0.3Sb sample.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elements mapping of Ir_{0.7}Rh_{0.3}Sb is displayed in Figure 1f and Figure S9... One can see that Ir, Rh, and Sb elements distribute homogenously over the sample.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern of Ir0.7Rh0.3Sb matches standard IrSb structure (PDF 65-3429) with high crystallinity confirmed by selected area electron diffraction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of Ir_{0.7}Rh_{0.3}Sb is illustrated in Figure S6... the peaks can be indexed to the standard structure of IrSb (powder diffraction file card No. 65-3429)... This pattern can be indexed to be along the zone axis of [100], with distinguished diffraction spots, which indicates the high crystallinity.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS shows Ir 4f7/2 at 60.0 eV and 4f5/2 at 63.0 eV in IrSb (slightly lower than Ir metal, indicating negative oxidation state); binding energy shifts +0.3 eV higher in Ir0.7Rh0.3Sb; Sb 3d5/2 at 528.1 eV (Sb0) and 530.1 eV (Sb3+), with increased Sb3+ proportion after Rh doping; Rh 3d5/2 at 306.9 eV in Ir0.7Rh0.3Sb (lower than Rh metal).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure 2a, the emerged peaks at 60.0 eV and 63.0 eV correspond to the Ir 4f_{7/2} and Ir 4f_{5/2} orbitals, respectively. The binding energy is slightly lower than that of Ir metal... By comparing... the binding energy increases by 0.3 eV for Ir_{0.7}Rh_{0.3}Sb... The deconvoluted peaks located at 528.1 eV and 530.1 eV in Figure 2c,d correspond to the Sb 3d_{5/2} orbitals of Sb^0 and Sb^{3+}... The Rh 3d_{5/2} peak in Ir_{0.7}Rh_{0.3}Sb is observed at 306.9 eV, which is lower than that in Rh metal.

nodes.characterization_summary: Normalized Ir L3-edge XANES (~11,215 eV) shows white line intensity: IrO2 (highest valence) > Ir0.7Rh0.3Sb > Ir foil > IrSb (negative valence); absorption edge energy Ir foil > IrSb.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3a shows the normalized Ir L_3 edge XANES... around 11 215 eV. ... Ir atoms in IrO_2 exhibit the highest valence state and also the highest white line intensity. The white line intensity of IrSb is weaker than that of Ir foil... the white line peak of Ir_{0.7}Rh_{0.3}Sb is stronger than that of IrSb and Ir foil. ... the absorption edge energy of Ir foil is larger than that of IrSb.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fourier-transformed k^2-weighted EXAFS shows Ir-M (M=Ir,Rh) at 2.51 Å, Ir-O at 1.57 Å, and Ir-Sb at 1.9 Å shells for IrSb and Ir0.7Rh0.3Sb.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The k^2-weighted Fourier transformation of the EXAFS... The peak at around 2.51 Å is assigned to the Ir-M (M=Ir, Rh) shells... For IrSb and Ir_{0.7}Rh_{0.3}Sb, an additional peak arises at around 1.9 Å, which can be assigned to the Ir-Sb shells.

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrical double layer capacitance Cdl values: IrSb 2.1 mF cm^-2, Ir0.2Rh0.8Sb 16.1 mF cm^-2, Ir0.7Rh0.3Sb 19.8 mF cm^-2, Ir0.6Rh0.4Sb 5.6 mF cm^-2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrical double layer capacitance (C_dl) was shown in Figure 4c... The Ir_{1-x}Rh_xSb alloy possesses a C_dl of 2.1, 16.1, 19.8, and 5.6 mF cm^{-2} with x = 0, 0.2, 0.3, and 0.4, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy shows Ir0.7Rh0.3Sb exhibits the smallest charge transfer resistance.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 4d presents the electrochemical impedance diagrams... It is found that the Ir_{0.7}Rh_{0.3}Sb exhibits the smallest charge transfer resistance.

nodes.characterization_summary: Selected area electron diffraction pattern indexed to [100] zone axis with distinguished spots confirms high crystallinity of Ir1−xRhxSb.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Further, the selected area electron diffraction is measured, with pattern shown in Figure S12... This pattern can be indexed to be along the zone axis of [100], with distinguished diffraction spots, which indicates the high crystallinity of the prepared Ir_{1-x}Rh_xSb samples.
